AUTHOR: Wang
TITLE: DyFish-DETR: Underwater Fish Image Recognition Based on Detection Transformer
VENUE: JOURNAL OF MARINE SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
REGION: Zhujiang Park, Guangzhou, China (own); also Denmark (Brackish), Taiwan (F4K), RUOD
SPECIES: Koi, tilapia (own dataset); Brackish 6 classes; F4K 23 species
DATA: Own freshwater fish dataset (RGB cameras submerged in park water); Fish4Knowledge23, Brackish, RUOD (each trained/tested separately)
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'The created freshwater fish dataset contains multiple angles and parts of fish photographed under different brightness levels'
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'selecting 4691 images for our dataset. Following a ratio of 7:1:2, we divided the images into training sets, validation sets, and testing sets.'
R_EV: Sec. 4.4.2: model applied 'on three public underwater datasets separately'; each dataset trained and tested in-domain, no cross-dataset test.
E_EV: Table 2: only 'P, R, mAP50, mAP50:95' reported for the freshwater fish dataset.
ARCH: DyFish-DETR (RT-DETR with DyFishNet dynamic snake conv backbone + Slim Hybrid Encoder)
METR: P, R, mAP50, mAP50:95, COCO AP/AR, params, GFLOPs, FPS
NOTE: Own data: koi/tilapia in Zhujiang Park water ('real natural water environment'); park pond is semi-natural; Brackish (monitoring dataset) results also reported, supporting INCL=Y. Split unit for headline own dataset stated as images, randomness not explicit. 'Different brightness levels' is the only visibility-related statement on own data (V3=Y, weak). RUOD has fog/colour/light challenge test sets but results per challenge set not reported.
